convoLines.text: "Do you ever just need to be alone? Like, really alone?"
"Okay." Something shutters, just slightly.
"Still on needing to be alone."
"I can't. Not today. Ask me when the work's done."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Same time tomorrow, maybe."
"I've been turning something over. What do YOU think actually happened to us?"
"That's where I keep landing too. The question is what it wants."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on what you think happened to us. Simple as that."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
It's quiet at the trap line. Roman doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"We went over this," Roman says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Roman grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
Roman looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Same time tomorrow, maybe."
"Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"Fine." Their face closes like a door.
"Still on your read on people here. You'd know about that."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "The whole fire was arguing about The Moderator last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Ugly Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"I'm staying out of the naming fight. For now. Someone always gets precious about their pick."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Have you heard? No? Good, I get to tell you first."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Okay, so — Hassan talks to the garden. The garden listens. I've seen it. Don't say I told you."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that news."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"...I need to go be quiet for a while."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part."
"Right." They look away, and the question dies where it stood.
"Still on the talking-to-strangers part."
"Birds went quiet an hour before it spoke the first time. They knew. Animals always know first."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Marek is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
You show them Chickweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Okay, so — something happened this morning."
"Okay, so — Mara? An army medic, back before. Solid person. Don't say I told you."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Marek nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"The treeline, this morning — something moved out there, big. By the time I looked properly it was gone. But I saw it."
"As I said — we're still on that news."
They let the words sit there, unanswered.
"I'll keep it to myself. What's on your mind?"
"Good question." "The Informant. They just... took Mara and Hassan. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
You show them Greenbrier Shoots — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Hey — I found some Chickweed today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson."
"Okay, I'm all ears."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "They took you — The Moot, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.

"Sure. I'll be around."

"Noted. Filing that under 'extremely useful.' The village needs that."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on what you're good at."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Pavel shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
A flicker at the corner of their mouth. Not quite a smile. Not quite anything.
"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Anchorage, Alaska. I keep my head down. Old habit. It kept me alive before; it keeps me alive now."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Pavel rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."

"That again?" Pavel sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
Pavel looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"See you around."

"Still on what got you through the first week."

"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Listen. I need you to hear this before you go back out there."
"You've seen what's out there. I'm just saying — the treeline at dusk. Don't."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Good. I mean it — watch yourself out there."
"It's nothing, really. What were you saying?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "Have you felt it? Like the air before a storm, but — bigger. Something's on its way."
They nod. "Okay."
"My part? I keep the fire lit where it sits. Somebody should tend the waiting."
"Alright — I should get back to it."

"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Water's almost gone — 2 liters. I can't carry enough alone. First light, the creek, you and me?"
"I checked the cistern three times hoping I misread it. 2 liters. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."

"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."

"Still on what's been happening."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
"Fine." Their face closes like a door.
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on where you're from."
Whatever warmth was building cools to politeness.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"Fine." Sharp. "You want to hear it? I dug it up. I was starving and your hole was right there. Happy now?"
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Right. Go on, then."
"Take care out there."
"You said something took us. Something big. I keep watching the sky since you said it."
They grin when they spot you — unguarded, for once.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that personal stuff. How are you holding up, though?"
They nod — and keep their distance, for now.
"Okay, I'm all ears."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "They say the table's coming. For us. I keep thinking about what we'd even bring to it."
"Seven doors and it chose US. I braid grass while listening to plans and try to feel chosen instead of chosen-at."

"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You asked why I wanted to know, about your first memory. Fair question. I'm still curious, if you ever feel like telling it."
There's an ease between you now — the kind that takes weeks to build.

"Still on that personal stuff."

"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Brooklyn Nikolaev is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Brooklyn Nikolaev is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Brooklyn kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Brooklyn's gone." Aurora looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Brooklyn." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Dwayne blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
